C_capabilities.description_what_how: The supplied endpoint returns HTTP 401 on unauthenticated POST and advertises scopes mcp:query, mcp:manage, and mcp:implement. Optimizely documents eight tools for its separately named Experimentation endpoint. No tool list for the supplied endpoint was found; the eight documented tools are best-available product evidence, not confirmed input-endpoint tools.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: The unauthenticated endpoint returned JSON-RPC error code -401 with message "Authentication required: OAuth authorization needed." Authenticated tool result formats were not found.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth-protected resource metadata: bearer token in header; scopes_supported are exactly ["mcp:query", "mcp:manage", "mcp:implement"]. Endpoint POST returned HTTP 401 and WWW-Authenticate referenced the resource metadata URL. Official Experimentation setup documents an OAuth 2.0 browser flow. The authorization server metadata could not be fetched in the provided evidence (DNS lookup failure), so registration endpoint, PKCE, grant types, token authentication methods, token lifetime, and revocation are NOT FOUND.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Read/write: official Experimentation docs list query/reporting/SDK lookup and entity lifecycle tools; lifecycle supports create, update, and archive. No annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) were published. 2. Docs say the agent confirms target project, environment, and details before committing; this is described as agent behavior, with no published server-enforced confirmation parameter or flow. 3. Supplied endpoint metadata lists mcp:query, mcp:manage, mcp:implement and header bearer auth. Official Experimentation docs say it uses the user’s Optimizely identity and existing permissions. Admin enablement and connected instance requirements are documented for that other endpoint; token lifetime is described as time-limited, exact duration NOT FOUND. 4. No read-only mode, tool filter, query-free mode, or environment endpoint option documented; docs mention querying/comparing environments. Separate Experimentation and Analytics endpoints are documented. 5. Official docs say the MCP server sees the same projects, experiments, and data accessible in the UI; MCP-specific masking or PII exclusion NOT FOUND. 6. MCP-specific rate limits, quotas, bulk caps, truncation, and per-call costs NOT FOUND; Experimentation setup says MCP use does not consume Mark credits. 7. Input validation, unknown-argument behavior, coercion, corrections, and operator overrides NOT FOUND. 8. MCP-call logging, audit trails, and telemetry NOT FOUND. 9. No feedback, rating, survey, report-to-vendor, or upsell tool identified in the eight official names/descriptions; no input-endpoint tool list exists to inspect. 10. Official examples recommend specifying project scope and describe the agent confirming target and details; confirmation is not shown as server-enforced. Examples also say an editor agent may search local code, and that code is not sent to Optimizely. 11. Documentation says the agent maintains context within a conversation; no evidence that prior behavior changes server outputs or persists across conversations. 12. No architecture for the supplied endpoint is published. Officially documented sibling Experimentation and Analytics servers use separate URLs. 13. No raw API request, arbitrary SQL, script execution, or universal escape-hatch tool appears in the published eight-tool list.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Official Experimentation docs recommend confirming project, environment, and details before changes. The documentation does not show this as a server-enforced rule. The examples also advise naming the project to reduce ambiguity.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Official Experimentation documentation says the server sees the same projects, experiments, and data the user can access in the UI, and that permissions carry over. Product Use Terms state customer data will not be used to train, develop, or improve GenAI features for the benefit of others. These statements are not specific to the supplied endpoint.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Optimizely says MCP access uses the user’s Optimizely identity and existing permissions. Its product terms state customer data is not used to train or improve GenAI features for others. The Experimentation server is described as available to Experimentation customers without separate sign-up or waitlist.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The endpoint’s OAuth metadata provides evidence of authentication and scopes. No public code or operational documentation establishes that the input endpoint enforces the documentation’s permission, confirmation, data-use, or retention statements. Confirmation is described as agent behavior; no server-side enforcement mechanism is documented.

contradictions: The supplied endpoint is https://mcp.optimizely.com/mcp, while official Experimentation setup and overview documentation direct clients to https://exp.mcp.opal.optimizely.com/mcp. The supplied endpoint has its own OAuth protected-resource metadata and scopes, but no official source found here identifies its product or tools.

The supplied endpoint advertises scopes mcp:query, mcp:manage, and mcp:implement. The official Experimentation endpoint documentation groups capabilities as Query, Manage, and Implement but does not publish these scopes or establish that it is the same endpoint.

APIs.io labels the supplied endpoint “Episerver”; the official Experimentation documentation instead identifies the exp.mcp.opal.optimizely.com endpoint. The APIs.io listing provides no tool list and is not used to establish official tools.
observations_for_research: The scope names on the supplied endpoint map closely to the three categories documented for the Experimentation MCP, but endpoint identity is not established.

The official Experimentation tool list separates reporting queries from ordinary experimentation queries and SDK documentation lookup, alongside an entity lifecycle tool that can create, update, and archive.
The official documentation describes confirmation as an agent step, but does not specify a server-enforced approval mechanism.
Official setup documentation states MCP use does not consume Mark credits; product plans and pricing are individually packaged.
